papers.title: Beyond Final Scores: A Systematic Evaluation of Agents for Long-Horizon AI Research and Development
papers.abstract: Abstract Frontier autonomous agents excel at engineering optimization but show unstable performance, limited novelty, and variable experience reuse across long-horizon tasks.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Autonomous agents are increasingly capable of improving models, systems, and other technical artifacts through long-horizon experimentation. To understand the current state of this capability, however, evaluation must go beyond final scores, which neither reveal where progress is gained or lost nor indicate whether accumulated experience improves later decisions. We therefore present a systematic evaluation of seven frontier models on 36 long-horizon tasks based on a new framework that uses rule-based metrics to characterize within-run behavior through Solution Framing, Execution, and Feedback Control and controlled comparisons to assess experience reuse within and across tasks. The results show that current agents operate more like engineering optimizers than fully autonomous researchers: they can formulate and implement practical solutions, but their performance varies substantially across runs, their strongest solutions mainly adapt or combine established techniques, and genuine methodological novelty remains rare. Detailed analysis reveals that observed performance is shaped by multiple factors, including distinct process bottlenecks behind similar final outcomes, experience reuse that can help or mislead subsequent decisions, and harness designs that affect performance stability. These findings suggest concrete directions for improving model training, inference-time strategies, experience management, and harness design.
affiliations: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

ru.title: От оптимизаторов к исследователям: оценка автономных агентов в долгосрочных экспериментах
ru.desc: В работе проводится систематическая оценка семи передовых языковых моделей на 36 сложных многошаговых задачах инженерной оптимизации. Авторы предлагают новую схему оценки, использующую правила для анализа поведения агентов на этапах формулирования решения, его реализации и обратной связи. Результаты показывают, что современные агенты работают скорее как оптимизаторы, чем полностью автономные исследователи: они могут формулировать решения, но показывают нестабильную производительность и редко генерируют новые методологии. Исследование выявляет различные факторы, влияющие на качество работы, включая узкие места процесса, переиспользование опыта и влияние конструкции системы на стабильность.

en.title: Enhancing Stability and Novelty in Autonomous Agents
en.desc: This paper evaluates the performance of advanced autonomous agents in engineering optimization tasks. It highlights that while these agents can generate solutions, their performance is inconsistent and often relies on existing techniques rather than innovative methods. The study introduces a new evaluation framework that assesses agents based on their behavior during task execution, focusing on aspects like Solution Framing and Feedback Control. The findings indicate that improvements in training and design are necessary to enhance the agents' stability and novelty in long-horizon tasks.

zh.title: 提升自主代理的稳定性与创新性
zh.desc: 本论文探讨了前沿自主代理在工程优化中的表现，指出其在长时间任务中的性能不稳定、创新性有限和经验重用不均。研究通过一个新的评估框架，对七个前沿模型在36个长时间任务上的表现进行了系统评估，使用基于规则的指标来分析代理的行为。结果显示，当前的代理更像是工程优化者，而非完全自主的研究者，虽然能够制定和实施实用解决方案，但其表现因运行而异，且真正的方法创新仍然稀少。研究还揭示了影响性能的多个因素，包括相似最终结果背后的过程瓶颈、经验重用对后续决策的影响，以及设计对性能稳定性的影响。

papers.title: Marionette: Predicting World States, Rendering Geometry, Painting Appearance
papers.abstract: Abstract Marionette predicts explicit 3D articulated world states for interactive games, uses a fixed renderer for geometry, and synthesizes video via diffusion, enabling direct state-level control and long-horizon consistency repair.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Interactive game world models typically autoregress visual observations directly in pixel or latent space, forcing structured properties such as pose, geometry, and occlusion to be implicitly maintained by the same generative sequence. Over long horizons, errors in these latent world properties accumulate, making consistency and controllability fragile. We explicitly model the evolving world state, delegate exact geometric computation to a fixed, zero-parameter renderer, and leave the neural model to synthesize appearance. We instantiate this idea as Marionette, a world model for interactive games with articulated characters. First, a two-stage autoregressive dynamics model predicts an explicit and interpretable 276-dimensional 3D world state comprising multi-entity articulated skeletons, metric root trajectories, and rotations. Second, a zero-parameter graphics bridge converts the predicted state into pose-control videos, computing world-space geometry and occlusion in closed form. Third, a control-conditioned video-diffusion observation model synthesizes photorealistic RGB observations from the resulting structured controls. Our experiments establish two properties of Marionette. First, the predicted world state is directly controllable. Forcing a mismatched action stream changes root-aligned joint error by 31% across 48 held-out segments. Second, long-horizon behaviour is determined in the state, and can be repaired there. Left free, the two generated characters drift to 21.2 m apart (recorded sessions stay near 5 m) and a third of frames show ground penetration. Two rules imposed on the explicit state, a terrain collider and a separation cap, cut penetration by 66% and keep the pair engaged, with no change to the observation model. Routing appearance through the predicted state costs no fidelity we can detect, at an FVD of 831 against 799 for recorded pose.
affiliations: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

ru.title: Явное управление состоянием игрового мира через структурированный синтез
ru.desc: Marionette — это модель мира для интерактивных игр, которая явно предсказывает трёхмерное состояние с артикулированными персонажами вместо прямого синтеза пикселей. Архитектура состоит из трёх компонентов: авторегрессивная динамическая модель предсказывает 276-мерное состояние включающее скелеты, траектории и ротации; фиксированный графический рендер вычисляет геометрию и окклюзию в замкнутом виде; диффузионная модель синтезирует фотореалистичные наблюдения из полученных управлений. Такой подход позволяет напрямую контролировать предсказанное состояние и исправлять долгосрочные ошибки консистентности через простые правила без изменения модели наблюдений.

en.title: Marionette: Mastering 3D Control in Interactive Games
en.desc: The paper presents Marionette, a machine learning model designed for predicting 3D articulated states in interactive games. Unlike traditional methods that generate visual observations directly, Marionette explicitly models the evolving world state and uses a fixed renderer for geometry, which enhances control and consistency over long time horizons. It employs a two-stage autoregressive dynamics model to predict a detailed 276-dimensional world state, which includes articulated skeletons and trajectories. Additionally, a video-diffusion model synthesizes realistic visuals from this structured state, allowing for direct control and significant improvements in long-term behavior consistency.

zh.title: Marionette：互动游戏中的3D动态状态预测
zh.desc: Marionette 是一种用于互动游戏的世界模型，它能够预测明确的 3D 动态状态。该模型使用固定的渲染器进行几何计算，并通过扩散合成视频，从而实现直接的状态级控制和长期一致性修复。通过明确建模不断变化的世界状态，Marionette 能够有效地处理多实体的关节骨架和运动轨迹。实验表明，Marionette 的预测状态是可控的，并且能够在长时间内保持一致性。

papers.title: SPARGen: Unifying Spatial Perception and Reasoning through Native Multimodal Generation
papers.abstract: Abstract SPARGen unifies 3D reconstruction, dense correspondence, and spatial reasoning into a single instruction-conditioned multimodal generative model that jointly learns shared spatial representations.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Spatial perception and reasoning from visual observations require recovering geometric structure, establishing correspondences, and understanding spatial relations. Existing approaches typically address these capabilities separately using task-specific architectures or external geometric modules, limiting knowledge transfer among complementary representations of the same physical scene. We introduce SPARGen, a unified multimodal framework that casts 3D reconstruction, dense correspondence, and spatial reasoning as instruction-conditioned generation tasks. SPARGen serializes compact structured and linguistic outputs as token sequences while generating dense geometric fields in image-aligned forms, enabling spatial supervision to jointly shape shared representations within a native multimodal generative model. Experiments across benchmarks for 3D reconstruction, correspondence, and spatial reasoning show that SPARGen achieves competitive performance across heterogeneous spatial tasks within a single native multimodal generative framework.

ru.title: Единая генеративная модель для пространственного понимания сцен
ru.desc: SPARGen представляет собой единую мультимодальную генеративную модель, которая объединяет трёхмерную реконструкцию, установление плотного соответствия и пространственное рассуждение в одной архитектуре. Модель работает с инструкциями и совместно обучает общие пространственные представления, кодируя выходные данные в виде последовательностей токенов. В отличие от существующих подходов, которые используют отдельные специализированные архитектуры для каждой задачи, SPARGen позволяет знаниям передаваться между различными пространственными представлениями одной сцены. Экспериментальная оценка на эталонных наборах данных показывает, что модель достигает конкурентных результатов сразу по нескольким пространственным задачам в рамках одного обобщённого фреймворка.

en.title: Unifying 3D Tasks with SPARGen: One Model, Many Solutions
en.desc: SPARGen is a novel multimodal generative model that integrates 3D reconstruction, dense correspondence, and spatial reasoning into one framework. It learns shared spatial representations by treating these tasks as instruction-conditioned generation problems. This approach allows for better knowledge transfer between different spatial tasks, overcoming limitations of traditional methods that use separate architectures. Experiments demonstrate that SPARGen performs competitively across various benchmarks, showcasing its effectiveness in handling diverse spatial challenges.

zh.title: SPARGen：统一的多模态生成模型
zh.desc: SPARGen 是一个统一的多模态生成模型，将 3D 重建、密集对应和空间推理整合为一个指令条件生成任务。该模型通过学习共享的空间表示，解决了从视觉观察中恢复几何结构、建立对应关系和理解空间关系的问题。与传统方法不同，SPARGen 不再使用特定任务的架构或外部几何模块，而是将这些能力统一在一个框架内。实验结果表明，SPARGen 在多个空间任务上表现出色，展示了其在多模态生成模型中的竞争力。

papers.title: Intern-S2-Mobius: Foundation Model with Decoupled Knowledge and Reasoning
papers.abstract: Abstract Mobius-v0 separates global memory storage from iterative reasoning modules to improve knowledge compression and inference efficiency, yielding comparable performance with less training data and faster inference.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small We introduce Mobius-v0, an architecture that comprises a globally shared Memory (FFN) that stores knowledge vectors and multiple Reasoners (Self-Attn) that iteratively achieve compositional reasoning. Using hidden states as cache and carrier, reasoners repeatedly query memory for required knowledge-vectors, while the knowledge is transmitted back to reasoning operators. Through this knowledge-reasoning-separation architecture, Mobius achieves better knowledge compression and reasoning efficiency. Built upon Mobius-v0 architecture: 1) Our 7B model trained-from-scratch achieves similar downstream score as a 7B Transformer baseline with 62.6% of baseline's training data. 2) Our Intern-S2-Mobius, continually-pretrained from Qwen3.5-35B, achieves similar downstream score while delivering nearly 4x end-to-end inference speedup.

ru.title: Разделение памяти и логики для эффективного рассуждения
ru.desc: Авторы представляют Mobius-v0 — архитектуру, которая разделяет глобальную память (реализованную как FFN) для хранения векторов знаний и несколько модулей рассуждения (Self-Attention) для итеративного логического вывода. Модули рассуждения многократно обращаются к памяти за необходимыми векторами знаний, которые затем передаются обратно в операторы рассуждения через скрытые состояния. Благодаря такой архитектуре разделения знаний и рассуждений достигается лучшая компрессия знаний и эффективность вычислений. Модель показывает сравнимое качество на задачах при использовании меньше данных для обучения и обеспечивает ускорение вывода в 4 раза по сравнению с базовыми моделями Transformer.

en.title: Efficient Knowledge Handling with Mobius-v0
en.desc: Mobius-v0 is a new machine learning architecture that separates memory storage from reasoning processes to enhance efficiency in knowledge handling. It uses a globally shared memory to store knowledge vectors and multiple reasoning modules that work together to perform complex reasoning tasks. By allowing reasoners to query memory for necessary information, Mobius-v0 improves both knowledge compression and inference speed. The results show that Mobius-v0 can achieve comparable performance to traditional models while using significantly less training data and providing faster inference times.

zh.title: Mobius-v0：高效推理与知识压缩的新架构
zh.desc: Mobius-v0是一种新型架构，它将全局内存存储与迭代推理模块分开，从而提高了知识压缩和推理效率。该架构使用一个共享的内存（FFN）来存储知识向量，并通过多个推理器（Self-Attn）进行组合推理。推理器利用隐藏状态作为缓存，反复查询内存以获取所需的知识向量，并将知识传递回推理操作。通过这种知识与推理分离的架构，Mobius在使用更少的训练数据时，仍能实现与传统模型相当的性能，并加快了推理速度。

papers.title: Dion3: Full-Stack Orthogonal Updates
papers.abstract: Abstract Dion3 accelerates the Muon optimizer by reducing orthogonalization and communication overhead through algorithmic, kernel-level, and update-rule improvements.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small The Muon optimizer incurs a significant overhead cost due to its cubic-time Newton-Schulz orthogonalization step. When weights are sharded, communication overhead compounds this computational cost, eroding the benefits of Muon in many settings. We present Dion3, a revision of Muon that targets this overhead at every level of the stack. Our Gram Newton-Schulz algorithm reduces the FLOP cost of orthogonalization, our CuteDSL kernels accelerate it by exploiting symmetry, and our megabatching strategy reduces communication overhead. Moreover, we propose a simple change to the update rule that cuts costs even further: selecting only a fraction of the momentum matrix's rows to orthogonalize at each step. This update rule improves on Dion (another "compressed" version of Muon), in both speed and performance. Overall, Dion3 matches or improves on the loss achieved by Muon but reduces optimizer step time by up to 6x. Dion3 is available via the dion package (https://github.com/microsoft/dion) as a drop-in replacement for Muon.

ru.title: Шесть раз быстрее: оптимизатор Dion3 побеждает коммуникационные издержки
ru.desc: Статья представляет Dion3 — оптимизированную версию оптимизатора Muon, который значительно ускоряется за счёт снижения вычислительных затрат на ортогонализацию и коммуникационных издержек. Авторы вводят алгоритм Gram Newton-Schulz для уменьшения количества операций при ортогонализации, специализированные ядра CuteDSL для более быстрого выполнения вычислений, а также стратегию мегабатчинга для снижения коммуникационных затрат при распределённом обучении. Ключевым улучшением является модификация правила обновления, при котором ортогонализируется только часть строк матрицы импульса на каждом шаге, что обеспечивает дополнительное ускорение. Dion3 достигает качества обучения, сравнимого или лучшего, чем Muon, при этом сокращая время шага оптимизатора в 6 раз.

en.title: Dion3: Speeding Up Muon Optimization with Smart Improvements
en.desc: Dion3 is an enhanced version of the Muon optimizer that significantly reduces computational overhead associated with the orthogonalization process. It introduces a Gram Newton-Schulz algorithm that lowers the floating-point operations (FLOP) required for orthogonalization, while also utilizing CuteDSL kernels to speed up computations by taking advantage of symmetry. Additionally, Dion3 implements a megabatching strategy to minimize communication overhead when weights are distributed across multiple devices. By modifying the update rule to orthogonalize only a subset of the momentum matrix's rows, Dion3 achieves faster optimization times, improving performance by up to 6 times compared to the original Muon optimizer.

zh.title: Dion3：提升 Muon 优化器效率的革命性改进
zh.desc: Dion3 是一种改进的 Muon 优化器，通过算法、内核级和更新规则的改进，减少了正交化和通信开销。传统的 Muon 优化器在正交化步骤中存在显著的开销，尤其是在权重分片时，通信开销进一步加重了计算成本。Dion3 通过 Gram Newton-Schulz 算法和 CuteDSL 内核加速正交化，并采用大批量处理策略来降低通信开销。此外，Dion3 还通过选择动量矩阵的部分行进行正交化，进一步提高了速度和性能，优化器步骤时间最多减少了 6 倍。
